questions.question: How many journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet are Egyptian police arresting for allegedly spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt?
questions.item: Egyptian police are arresting six journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet, accusing them of spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt.

questions.question: How many people were wounded in a mass shooting at a high school in Turgutlu, Turkey, after which the perpetrator was arrested?
questions.item: Eleven people are wounded in a mass shooting at a high school in Turgutlu, Turkey. The perpetrator is arrested.

questions.question: According to Israeli defense minister Israel Katz, how many militants who took part in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, has the military killed?
questions.item: Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the military has killed 4,000 militants who took part in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023.

questions.question: How many civilians were killed during an armed attack by unknown individuals in Madegoua, Far North Region, Cameroon?
questions.item: Fifteen civilians are killed during an armed attack by unknown individuals in Madegoua, Far North Region, Cameroon.

questions.question: Until what date may former Malaysian prime minister Najib Razak serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, following the conditional pardon granted by King Sultan Ibrahim?
questions.item: King Sultan Ibrahim of Malaysia grants former prime minister Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, following his corruption conviction linked to 1MDB.

questions.question: In which city did Colombia open an embassy while also restoring its free trade agreement with Israel?
questions.item: Colombia opens an embassy in Jerusalem and restores its free trade agreement with Israel.

questions.question: Whose executive office denied journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico access to the White House and confiscated or disabled their press passes, citing coverage of his administration?
questions.item: United States president Donald Trump's executive office denies journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico access to the White House and confiscates or disables their press passes, citing their coverage of his administration.

questions.question: What bacterium caused the pneumonic plague that killed a lab worker at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia, leading to nearly 200 workers being quarantined?
questions.item: A lab worker in Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia, dies from a pneumonic plague caused by Yersinia pestis, with nearly 200 workers in quarantine.

questions.question: How many suspected illegal gold miners died in the custody of Nigeria's civil defence agency in Minna, Niger State, where survivors blamed overcrowding and poor ventilation?
questions.item: Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners die in custody of Nigeria's civil defence agency in Minna, Niger State. Survivors say overcrowding and poor ventilation caused breathing difficulties, while an intelligence report links the deaths to those conditions. The government orders an investigation.

questions.question: How many individuals and entities of Russia's military and industrial complex are targeted by the 22nd package of sanctions approved by the Council of the European Union?
questions.item: The Council of the European Union approves the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, targeting 1,569 individuals and entities of the country's military and industrial complex.

questions.question: How many people were injured when a bus overturned on a road near Iraquara, Bahia, Brazil, killing seven people?
questions.item: Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a bus overturns on a road near Iraquara, Bahia, Brazil.

questions.question: What is the name of the youngest known exoplanet, located approximately 450 light-years from Earth, whose existence was confirmed by astronomers using a coronagraph at the W.M. Keck Observatory in Mauna Kea, Hawaii?
questions.item: Astronomers confirm the existence of Elias 2-24 b, the youngest known exoplanet, which is less than one million years old and located approximately 450 light-years from Earth. The discovery was observed through the W.M. Keck Observatory in Mauna Kea, Hawaii, U.S., using a coronagraph.

questions.question: How many members of the Dawlah Islamiya and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters were killed in clashes with combined police and military forces in Tugunan, Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro, Philippines?
questions.item: A series of clashes, involving combined police and military forces and remaining wanted members of the Dawlah Islamiya and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters, erupts in Tugunan, Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro, Philippines. Seven members from both groups are killed.

questions.question: In which Ukrainian city did Russian forces launch a ballistic missile attack on two buses, killing at least 30 people and wounding 18 others?
questions.item: Russian forces launch a ballistic missile attack on two buses in the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, while 18 others are wounded.

questions.question: Which armed group's drone strike on homes and a mosque in Ad-Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan, killed four women?
questions.item: Four women are killed in a Rapid Support Forces drone strike on homes and a mosque in Ad-Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan.

questions.question: Under a deal reached by Denmark and the United States granting permanent basing, overflight, and access rights, on which island is the U.S. allowed to expand its military presence?
questions.item: Denmark and the United States reach a deal allowing the U.S. to expand its military presence in Greenland and granting permanent basing, overflight, and access rights, while barring non-NATO countries from establishing bases and restricting sensitive investments on the island.

questions.question: How many people were killed when Saudi Arabia's air force carried out an airstrike at a market in Taiz, Yemen?
questions.item: Saudi Arabia's air force carries out an airstrike at a market in Taiz, Yemen, killing seven people and wounding 40 more.

questions.question: In the race to become UN Secretary-General, which Costa Rican was reported in the lead in the latest informal poll after Chilean Michelle Bachelet withdrew?
questions.item: Chilean Michelle Bachelet announces that she is withdrawing from the race to become UN Secretary-General after losing support, and that in the latest informal poll, Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is reported in the lead.

questions.question: Which energy company's appeal to expand the Mount Pleasant coal mine in New South Wales was rejected by Australia's High Court over greenhouse gas emissions from exported coal?
questions.item: Australia's High Court rejects MACH Energy's appeal to expand the Mount Pleasant coal mine in New South Wales, finding that planning authorities failed to adequately consider greenhouse gas emissions from burning exported coal overseas.

questions.question: Who led the opposition that won 176 seats in the Riksdag, prompting Ulf Kristersson to announce his resignation as Prime Minister of Sweden?
questions.item: Ulf Kristersson announces his resignation as Prime Minister of Sweden after his right-wing bloc wins 173 seats in the Riksdag, compared to 176 won by the opposition, led by Magdalena Andersson.

questions.question: Which company unveiled the EXOBOT SUV and sedan in Saudi Arabia as its first electric vehicles in the country?
questions.item: Ceer Motors unveils the EXOBOT SUV and sedan in Saudi Arabia, its first electric vehicles in the country.

questions.question: How many years in prison did a court in Paris, France, sentence Loik Le Priol to for murdering former Argentine rugby union player Federico Martín Aramburú in 2022?
questions.item: A court in Paris, France, sentences Loik Le Priol to 26 years in prison and Romain Bouvier to 19 years for murdering former Argentine rugby union player Federico Martín Aramburú in 2022. Le Priol and Bouvier had links to the dissolved far-right group Groupe Union Défense.

questions.question: What is the name of the Togo-flagged oil tanker that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps hit as it attempted to pass the Strait of Hormuz, according to IRNA?
questions.item: The IRNA reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has hit the Togo-flagged oil tanker Trend as it attempted to pass the Strait of Hormuz.

questions.question: During an operation against illegal miners in Tambopata province, Madre de Dios, Peru, a shootout killed three gunmen and a police officer and wounded another officer; in which district did this take place?
questions.item: Three gunmen and a police officer are killed, and another officer is wounded, in a shootout during an operation against illegal miners in Inambari District, Tambopata province, Madre de Dios, Peru. Authorities seize 15 AKM rifles, a pistol, and five grenades.

questions.question: In which city did the 16th-century Codex Azcatitlan go on display after France loaned two of its folios?
questions.item: The 16th-century Codex Azcatitlan goes on display in Mexico City after France loaned two folios nearly two centuries after the manuscript left the country. Mexico continues seeking the codex's permanent return from France.

questions.question: Who was released from a prison in Mandaluyong, Philippines, after president Bongbong Marcos's absolute pardon of her was approved?
questions.item: Mary Jane Veloso is released from a prison in Mandaluyong, Philippines, after president Bongbong Marcos's absolute pardon of her was approved yesterday.

questions.question: In which city in Mecca Province was a Yemeni resident reported to be killed by debris from a drone?
questions.item: A Yemeni resident is reported to be killed by debris from a drone in Taif, Mecca Province.

questions.question: How many civilians were killed when the Ethiopian National Defense Force launched 21 airstrikes in Alamata, Tigray Region?
questions.item: The Ethiopian National Defense Force launches 21 airstrikes in Alamata, Tigray Region, killing 14 civilians and wounding 22 more. Two empty schools are also hit.

questions.question: How many Burmese nationals is Malaysia repatriating from immigration detention centres in the first phase of a programme covering 5,000 people?
questions.item: Malaysia begins repatriating about 1,500 Burmese nationals from immigration detention centres under the first phase of a programme covering 5,000 people.

questions.question: After Guinea banned single-use plastic water sachets, causing shortages and higher prices, what nationwide price ceiling was set for retail packs of several sizes of bottled water?
questions.item: Guinea sets nationwide price ceilings for bottled water after a ban on single-use plastic water sachets causes shortages and higher prices, with retail packs of several bottle sizes capped at 25,000 francs (US$2.84).

questions.question: Whom did United States president Donald Trump meet on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, in the first in-person meeting between the countries' leaders following the 2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela and capture of Nicolás Maduro?
questions.item: United States president Donald Trump and Venezuelan interim president Delcy Rodríguez meet on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, marking the first in-person meeting between the countries' leaders following the 2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela and capture of Nicolás Maduro.

questions.question: In which South Darfur city did the Sudanese military launch heavy nighttime airstrikes against Rapid Support Forces targets?
questions.item: The Sudanese military at night launches heavy airstrikes against Rapid Support Forces targets in Nyala, South Darfur.

questions.question: In which city did a relief crew safely land the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking?
questions.item: A Flydubai flight from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv, Israel, is landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, by a relief crew after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking.

questions.question: Which Australian prime minister said an OpenAI-deployed agent accessed public and restricted files on a Medicare database during testing in June?
questions.item: Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese says that an OpenAI-deployed agent accessed public and restricted files on a Medicare database during testing in June. OpenAI notified the government in September, while investigations continue into the breach.

questions.question: According to the National Hurricane Center, what did Tropical Depression Six strengthen into during an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño?
questions.item: The National Hurricane Center reports that Tropical Depression Six strengthened into Tropical Storm Fay amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño, becoming the sixth named storm of the season.

questions.question: At which venue in St. Louis, Missouri, United States, is the beatification ceremony for the late American Catholic prelate and Rochester Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen held?
questions.item: The beatification ceremony for the late American Catholic prelate and Rochester Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen is held at The Dome at America's Center in St. Louis, Missouri, United States.

questions.question: In the elections held in Bosnia on 2026-10-04, how many members of the House of Representatives did Bosnians vote to elect?
questions.item: Bosnians vote to elect the three members of the presidency and 42 members of the House of Representatives. Concurrent elections are also held in the Federation to elect 98 seats of the regional legislature and in Republika Srpska to elect the entity's president and the 83 seats of the respective legislature.

questions.question: In rugby union, which team defeated defending champions Fiji 20–15 in the final at Chichibunomiya Stadium in Tokyo to win their fourth Pacific Nations Cup title?
questions.item: In rugby union, hosts Japan win their fourth Pacific Nations Cup title after defeating the defending champions Fiji 20–15 in the final at Chichibunomiya Stadium in Tokyo.

questions.question: Which group claimed responsibility for the suicide car bombing outside a mosque inside a police station in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, that killed at least 31 people?
questions.item: A suicide car bombing outside a mosque located inside a police station in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, kills at least 31 people, including 16 policemen, and injures at least 100 more. The Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group claims responsibility.

questions.question: How many previously blocked news websites, including EFE, El Nacional, NTN24, and Semana, did Venezuela restore access to amid political transition talks?
questions.item: Venezuela restores access to 17 news websites that were previously blocked, including EFE, El Nacional, NTN24, and Semana, as the interim government and opposition resume political transition talks that include freedom of expression.

questions.question: Which town in North Kordofan did the Sudanese Armed Forces announce they had recaptured?
questions.item: The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have recaptured Sodri, North Kordofan.

questions.question: Which independent candidate won the 2026 Kraków mayoral election in Poland, defeating government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska?
questions.item: Independent candidate Łukasz Gibała wins the Kraków mayoral election in Poland against government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska.

questions.question: How many former Barclays traders had their convictions for manipulating Libor and Euribor quashed by the Court of Appeal in London, United Kingdom?
questions.item: The Court of Appeal in London, United Kingdom, quashes the convictions of five former Barclays traders for manipulating Libor and Euribor, following a 2025 Supreme Court ruling that found legal errors had made similar convictions unsafe.

questions.question: In which West Bank village did Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home, injuring another?
questions.item: Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home in Yasuf, West Bank, and injure another.

questions.question: Eighteen people were killed in a mass shooting carried out by eight gunmen at a tavern in which township in Gauteng, South Africa?
questions.item: Eighteen people are killed and 14 more are injured in a mass shooting carried out by eight gunmen at a tavern in Wedela township, Gauteng, South Africa. Police launch a manhunt for the gunmen. It is suspected that the shooting is linked to a dispute over illegal gold mining.

questions.question: Which Mexican state's authority to annul elections due to interference by organized crime was invalidated by the Supreme Court of Mexico, which instructed the local legislature to instead include annulment due to foreign interference?
questions.item: The Supreme Court of Mexico invalidates the state of Chihuahua's authority to annul elections due to interference by organized crime and instructs the local legislature to instead include the annulment of elections due to foreign interference.

questions.question: Which South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law"?
questions.item: South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law".

questions.question: In what city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, did a Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber self-detonate at a police checkpoint, killing twelve people and wounding 30 more?
questions.item: A Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber self-detonates at a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing twelve people and wounding 30 more.

questions.question: Which former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister was among the hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf members detained after the federal government suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and imposed emergency rule?
questions.item: Pakistan's federal government detains hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members, including former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial officials, after suspending the PTI-led provincial administration and imposing emergency rule.

questions.question: How many men did Sri Lanka's High Court convict for involvement in the 2019 Easter bombings?
questions.item: Sri Lanka's High Court convicts 15 men involved in the Easter bombings in 2019.
